articles.title: Pakistan cricket chaos prompts stand-in to seek swift reset after royal appointment
articles.summary: Mike Hesson had only been in the UK to meet the king. Interim picks up the pieces after seven players sent home. Mike Hesson was only in the UK this week to meet King Charles.
body: Even by Pakistan’s standards, this past week has been more than a little chaotic, with their somewhat nuclear response to going 2-0 down to England the talk of the sport. Hesson, previously Pakistan’s white-ball coach, has been parachuted in to restore some pride in the third Test at Edgbaston that starts next week.

“It’s been pretty challenging,” said Hesson, who had been in Japan preparing for the Asian Games before a supposed whistle-stop visit to Clarence House with the Pakistan Cricket Board on Wednesday turned into a brand new role. “I was heading over to see the king and be part of a nice occasion. That got expedited.”

After holding one-on-one talks with the remaining squad members this week, and then drilling them at Edgbaston’s indoor school due to rain, Hesson believes a reset has occurred. Of the seven players being flown in, three were still due to arrive in the UK on Friday. As for the departed, Hesson tried his best to explain.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s double-double helps USA rout China in Fiba World Cup opener
articles.summary: Clark finishes with 14 points and 11 assists. Americans extend World Cup win streak to 31. China’s 7ft 3in Zhang Ziyu scores 13 on debut. Caitlin Clark had 14 points and 11 assists to help the United States beat China, who were led by 7ft 3in Zhang Ziyu, 94-61 in their Fiba Women’s Basketball World…
body: Rhyne Howard also scored 14 points and Jackie Young added 12 for the Americans, who have now won 31 consecutive World Cup games dating back to a loss in the semi-final game of the 2006 tournament.

This a period of transition for the US with a young roster that includes the trio of Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese. None of them were in the starting lineup, but they were on the court together to close out the opening quarter, which the Americans dominated to go up 27-14.

China fought back at the start of the second quarter behind Zhang. The 19-year-old, who was making her first World Cup appearance, towered over the Americans. On defense, she stood under the basket, making it difficult for the US to score inside or get second shots off misses. On offense, the Americans constantly double-teamed her when she caught the ball.

Zhang’s first basket of the game got China within 33-25 with 6:21 left in the half. The US then went on a 16-4 run to close the first half up 49-29. Young had a three-point play and Breanna Stewart scored the final four points of the spurt.

articles.title: Kretinsky to become largest West Ham shareholder
articles.summary: Daniel Kretinsky says West Ham have been provided with much-needed certainty after it was confirmed he will become the club's largest shareholder.
body: Kretinsky has struck a deal with the Hammers' remaining shareholders, including former chairman David Sullivan, over the 25% of the club owned by the Gold family that will take his stake up to 46%.
The deal has ended former Newcastle director Amanda Staveley's immediate hopes of investing in the Championship club.
"I am deeply honoured to have the opportunity to become the largest shareholder of this great club," said Czech businessman Kretinsky.
"I appreciate the responsibility this brings and do not take it lightly.

articles.title: Dangerfield bends AFL elimination final to his will as Geelong end Carlton’s fairytale run
articles.summary: Cats defeat Blues 14.23 (107) to 11.8 (74) at the MCG. Veteran kicks five goals to set up semi-final showdown with Dockers. Sign up for our free weekly AFL newsletter.
body: Geelong used to be notorious for being asleep at the wheel after a bye, and for about 45 minutes last night it looked like it might cost them an AFL elimination final. They were dragging their heels, badly beaten up around the ball and missing shots they would normally gobble up. When Carlton jumped out to a 21-point lead, they had the 10 leading possession winners on the ground.

But the Cats finally got some cohesion and fluidity in their game, with their fleet of small-to-medium hybrid players – Gryan Miers and Brad Close in particular – finding space and using the ball well. As the rain teemed down and the legs got heavier, Geelong began to look like the superior side. And Patrick Dangerfield began to bend the elimination final to his will.

Dangerfield had been a crucial player when Carlton dominated early. His snap around his body in the first term – in the same part of the ground where he terrorised Hawthorn in the preliminary final last year – helped keep the Cats in the contest. But he was magnificent in the second half.

articles.title: Chaotic Crystal Palace transfer window leaves Pierre Sage to run the gamut of emotions
articles.summary: Manager was frustrated not to land defensive targets and lost last-day tug of war but can draw on positives as he seeks his first points. At least Pierre Sage did his research before joining Crystal Palace in June.
body: Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta ended up staying at Selhurst Park despite interest from Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively, while Palace brought in four new players after missing out to Sunderland for Malick Fofana in one of deadline day’s most dramatic storylines. But Sage is sanguine about experiencing a typically chaotic first transfer window in south London, and relieved to be able to concentrate on events on the pitch before Saturday’s trip to Fulham.

“I knew that and I had to deal and adapt to that,” Sage said when asked about Palace’s reputation for doing late deals, a trend that has led to them signing 10 players on the final day in the past three summer windows. “But at the end the most important thing is to have the player or the profile we choose and that’s the case. I think we are in line with what we need.”

articles.title: Gasly loses Monaco podium after McLaren and Red Bull win appeals
articles.summary: McLaren and Red Bull win their appeals against the result of the Monaco Grand Prix after a controversy over multiple incorrect pit-lane speeding penalties.
body: The victory means Alpine's Pierre Gasly loses the podium he was awarded after an appeal by his French team that overturned two five-second penalties.
Gasly, who finished third on the road, is dropped back to the seventh place he received in the official results.
Alpine, unlike the other teams involved, did not serve the penalties in the race because they believed they had been applied incorrectly.
Red Bull's Isack Hadjar is returned to third place and McLaren's Oscar Piastri fourth, with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad moving up to fifth and sixth.

articles.title: Moyes lives with disappointment after deadline day
articles.summary: Everton manager David Moyes accepts he has "to live with disappointments" after admitting he wanted to do more business on transfer deadline day.
body: A move for Monaco striker Folarin Balogun collapsed after the 25-year-old changed his mind following a medical at the club's Finch Farm training base.
The United States international emerged as a late target after Guinea-Bissau striker Beto completed a permanent switch to Serie A club Fiorentina.
The Toffees also explored deals for Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee and Aston Villa frontman Tammy Abraham but were unable to convince either to join.
They did sign Jack Grealish on a season-long loan deal from Manchester City, but lost star attacker Iliman Ndiaye to City in a deal worth £65m.

articles.title: Garcia vs Benn: Start time, undercard and how to watch fight
articles.summary: Expect fireworks as Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn prepare to clash next weekend, in a battle of two of boxing’s most-divisive stars. American welterweight Garcia puts the WBC title on the line against Britain’s Benn, with the pair headlining in Las Vegas.
body: Both men draw mixed reactions from fans of the sport, and both have returned adverse drug-test results in recent years. Still, they find themselves topping the bill in a huge fight, as Garcia makes his first defence of his world title, while Benn challenges for a major belt for the first time.

Benn, 30, enters the bout on the back of a points win against ex-champion Regis Prograis in April, and a decision victory over bitter rival Chris Eubank Jr, who previously handed Benn his sole professional loss.

Meanwhile, 28-year-old Garcia won the WBC strap by dropping and outpointing Mario Barrios in February, bouncing back from an upset loss to Rolly Romero. “King Ryan”’s only other defeat came in 2023, when he was stopped to the body by Gervonta Davis.

Garcia vs Benn will take place on Saturday 12 September at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. The main card will begin at 1am BST on Sunday (5pm PT / 7pm CT / 8pm ET on Saturday), with main-event ring walks following at around 4am BST (8pm PT / 10 CT / 11pm ET on Saturday).

The Los Angeles Lakers don't have many trade assets, but they do have a player or two they could still move.
body: One guy who keeps popping up in trade rumors is Jarred Vanderbilt, an athletic wing who isn't much of an offensive player.

Vanderbilt has never been a great shooter, shooting below 30% in three of his four seasons in Los Angeles. He's also dealt with some injury history throughout his career, playing in 29 games in 2023-24 and 36 in 2024-25.
It's tough to find a perfect trade for the Lakers to make involving him because of the limited assets they have to attach to a trade involving him and his contract.
However, it still sounds like the Lakers are attempting to do so.

articles.title: Russell tops second practice as Mercedes respond to Ferrari at Monza
articles.summary: George Russell beat Charles Leclerc to the fastest time of second practice at the Italian Grand Prix as Mercedes responded to Ferrari's early pace at Monza.
body: At an event in which championship-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli will start at the back of Sunday's grid owing to engine-change penalties, Russell has a big chance to eat into the Italian's 59-point advantage if he can deliver a strong race weekend.

Ferrari had finished first and second quickest in opening practice as they debuted an upgraded engine but Russell was the driver to beat in the second session amid continued sweltering temperatures in northern Italy.
The Briton set a quickest lap of 1:22.559 to outpace Leclerc - who had a late spin - by 0.120s and Antonelli by 0.141s.
Lewis Hamilton, second fastest in the earlier running, slipped to fifth behind McLaren's Lando Norris during a session which included the Ferrari running straight on at the first chicane.

articles.title: Arrow gets emotional farewell on 100th Rabbitohs appearance after MND diagnosis
articles.summary: Jai Arrow made an emotional 100th NRL appearance for the South Sydney Rabbitohs to mark his farewell from the sport, following his Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis.
body: Special dispensation had been granted by the NRL and Rabbitohs to allow Arrow the opportunity to take to the field for the opening kick-off another two times, with the game against Sydney Roosters marking a century of appearances.
Arrow walked his team out onto the field for the Sydney derby, with 'Stand By Me' playing before 'You'll Never Walk Alone' then rang around the Allianz Stadium.

The 31-year-old forward had made 178 appearances overall in the NRL before his retirement announcement earlier his year, playing at Brisbane Broncos and then Gold Coast Titans ahead of joining the Rabbitohs in 2021.
Arrow, also having featured 12 times for Queensland in State of Origin, fought back tears as he was presented to the crowd, who all stood in applause, many holding up banners of support in his name.

body: ALMERAQ is on a retrieval mission after flopping in the July Cup, but he can clinch his second Group 1 of the season in the Betfair Sprint Cup (3.40) at Haydock Park on Saturday.
A combination of the fast ground on an undulating track may have been his downfall at Newmarket, but my husband Tom [Marquand] reports his mount fresh and well for an assignment he should relish.
Shadwell's colt came of age in the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot and has proven form on soft ground, which I expect will bring the best out of him.

Clive Cox's Coppull looked a colt going places when stepping up to seven furlongs to win the Hungerford Stakes at Newbury and arrives at Haydock in rude health. He's a Group 1 winner in waiting but he's never encountered soft ground before which will raise a question mark if he takes his chance.
